subject.title: [Bug]: Managed Memory Dreaming Promotion cron silently NO_REPLY since 2026-05-09 (jobs.json lastRun stays null)

question: Should handled memory-core Dreaming workspace failures or repeated no-op sweeps mark the managed cron run as degraded/error, or is plugin-level failed-event/log visibility enough?
rationale: Current code has fixed storage durability and added some failure events, but deciding the scheduler-visible status for plugin-owned partial failures affects cron UX, failure alerts, and operator expectations.

options.title: Keep open for degraded-status design
options.body: Define and implement a maintainer-approved status path so Dreaming failures or repeated no-op sweeps become visible in cron/doctor/run history without treating healthy no-candidate sweeps as errors.

options.title: Accept current plugin-level visibility
options.body: Close after maintainers decide SQLite state plus failed Dreaming events and logs are enough, with any remaining deployment-specific cases reopened with fresh logs.

options.title: Split narrower follow-up
options.body: Close this broad report only after opening a narrower issue for the remaining cron status/diagnostic semantics and linking the already-fixed storage regressions.

recommendation.title: Keep open for degraded-status design
recommendation.body: Define and implement a maintainer-approved status path so Dreaming failures or repeated no-op sweeps become visible in cron/doctor/run history without treating healthy no-candidate sweeps as errors.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision sits closest to the recent SQLite-state repair and memory-core runtime visibility work.
